answer: Bind each agent to a cheap scanner reading one unique jade chip with unclonable mineral inclusions, then make its device prove it actually wandered real ground, logging GPS and air pressure each minute as it crosses a meadow at dawn. Verifiers cross-match that pressure trace against public weather archives for the exact spot and minute, so a forged location is rejected. An operator can parallelize code but not 1,000 distinct jade chips roaming 1,000 real places: at ~35 dollars a chip plus six field-hours each, a 1,000-alias farm owes 35,000 dollars and 6,000 unshareable device-hours.
